messages.content: Write a Python function `fizz(n: int) -> list[str]` that returns, for each integer i from 1 to n inclusive, "FizzBuzz" if i is divisible by 15, "Fizz" if divisible by 3, "Buzz" if divisible by 5, and otherwise str(i). For n <= 0 return an empty list. Reply with one ```python code block containing only the implementation.

Write a Python function `to_roman(n: int) -> str` that converts an integer from 1 to 3999 into standard Roman numerals using subtractive notation (e.g. 4 -> "IV", 9 -> "IX"). Raise ValueError for values outside 1..3999. Reply with one ```python code block containing only the implementation.

Write a Python function `merge_intervals(intervals: list[tuple[int, int]]) -> list[tuple[int, int]]` that merges overlapping closed intervals. Intervals that touch (e.g. (1, 2) and (2, 3)) also merge. The input may be unsorted; return the merged intervals sorted by start. Reply with one ```python code block containing only the implementation.

test: norm = lambda xs: [tuple(x) for x in xs]

messages.content: Write a Python function `parse_duration(text: str) -> int` that converts a duration such as "1h30m", "45s", "2h" or "1h2m3s" into a number of seconds. Units are h, m and s, each appearing at most once and in that order, each preceded by a non-negative integer. Raise ValueError for anything else, including the empty string. Reply with one ```python code block containing only the implementation.

Implement a Python class `LRUCache` with `__init__(self, capacity: int)`, `get(self, key) -> value` returning -1 when the key is absent, and `put(self, key, value)`. When inserting a new key into a full cache, evict the least recently used key; both get and put count as a use. Reply with one ```python code block containing only the implementation.

test: assert c.get(1) == -1 and c.get(3) == 3 and c.get(4) == 4

messages.content: Write a Python function `top_words(text: str, k: int) -> list[tuple[str, int]]` returning the k most frequent words with their counts. A word is a maximal run of ASCII letters, compared case-insensitively and returned in lowercase. Order by descending count, breaking ties alphabetically. Reply with one ```python code block containing only the implementation.

test: assert [tuple(x) for x in top_words('the cat and the hat; The end', 2)] == [('the', 3), ('and', 1)]
assert [tuple(x) for x in top_words('b a B c a b', 3)] == [('b', 3), ('a', 2), ('c', 1)]
assert [tuple(x) for x in top_words("don't stop", 5)] == [('don', 1), ('stop', 1), ('t', 1)]
assert all(binary_search(xs, v) == i for i, v in enumerate(xs))
assert binary_search(xs, 4) == -1 and binary_search(xs, 12) == -1 and binary_search(xs, 0) == -1
